sections.markdown:
## C2 - Confusables and KG hints, Chapter Two Keep your license

FACT_ID: sec02-R01 | anchor: A01
Suspension borrows the license back after a wait while revocation destroys it and forces reapplication, and junior violations stack sixty-day clocks whereas texting jumps straight to one hundred twenty days [A01].
Why it matters: group sanctions; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec02-F01, sec02-F02 [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=19]

FACT_ID: sec02-R02 | anchor: A02
Out-of-state convictions vanish except Ontario and Quebec, yet ignoring any out-of-state ticket still suspends, so recording and answering are opposite rules [A02].
Why it matters: group out-of-state; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec02-F06, sec02-F07 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=20]

FACT_ID: sec02-R03 | anchor: A03
Zero Tolerance punishes the low band from point-zero-two to point-zero-seven with six months off, while refusing its test costs a full year, so refusal dwarfs the underlying sip [A03].
Why it matters: group zero-tolerance; difficulty high; prereq sec02-F11; confusables sec02-F13 [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=21]

FACT_ID: sec02-R04 | anchor: A03
Refusals scale with age and history from one year to eighteen months to until-twenty-one, while violations scale with substance from ninety-day DWAI suspension up to year-long aggravated revocation [A03].
Why it matters: group alcohol-ladder; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec02-F10, sec02-F11 [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=21]

FACT_ID: sec02-R05 | anchor: A01
Junior sanctions fire per violation pattern while adult probation watches a six-month window, and both ladders end in revocation only after repeated failure [A01].
Why it matters: group sanctions; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec02-F02, sec02-F03 [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=19]

FACT_ID: sec02-R06 | anchor: A04
Eleven points in twenty-four months suspends by mail with identity-only hearings, while six points in eighteen months bills money instead, two point clocks with two different teeth [A04].
Why it matters: group points; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec02-F20, sec02-F28 [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=22]

FACT_ID: sec02-R07 | anchor: A05
Alcohol convictions bill two hundred fifty yearly for three years regardless of points, while point totals bill one hundred plus twenty-five per extra point yearly, so the same driver can owe on both tracks [A05].
Why it matters: group assessments; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec02-F27, sec02-F28 [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=23]

FACT_ID: sec02-R08 | anchor: A05
No-insurance revocations pair a year off with a seven-hundred-fifty-dollar penalty, while refusals pair revocation with five hundred, or seven hundred fifty on a five-year repeat [A05].
Why it matters: group penalties; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec02-F15, sec02-F26 [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=23]

FACT_ID: sec02-R09 | anchor: A04
The crash course erases points and premiums but never halts a mandatory sanction, banks no future credit, and shrinks no assessment, so relief and rescue differ [A04].
Why it matters: group courses; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec02-F21 [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=22]

FACT_ID: sec02-R10 | anchor: A05
Driving suspended is criminal with fines, jail risk and seizure, and twenty ignored-ticket suspensions make it criminal even for a non-driver, so the count itself becomes the crime [A05].
Why it matters: group suspended-driving; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec02-F29 [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=23]
